subject: Clearer Specification of MSstatsQC Input File Format

messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Clearer Specification of MSstatsQC Input File Format
parts: The documentation states "The recommended format includes Acquired Time, Peptide name, Annotations and data for any QC metrics such as Retention Time, Total Peak Area and Mass Accuracy etc." What other features of the data can MSstatsQC utilise that are referred to by "etc."? This format is described as "recommended", so what are the necessary columns and other optional columns which can be provided to calculate more metrics? Are there plans to make it more generally applicable to other kinds of proteomics, such as SWATH-MS data, by allowing more input data formats, such as output files created by OpenSWATH?

messages.author: bc24366d9dd67950
messages.subject: Re: Clearer Specification of MSstatsQC Input File Format
parts:
Dear Dario,

Thanks for following up. MSstatsQC input format requires Acquired Time, Peptide name, and Annotations columns as three necessary input columns. After Annotations,you can parse any metric of interest depending on the workflow you obtain QC data. Retention time, peak area and mass accuracy are just examples generated from Skyline output. MSstatsQC focuses on data analysis rather than calculating metrics.

We are currently expanding MSstatsQC for DDA outputs and SWATH-MS is another possible direction. Please let me know if there is any available QC outputs generated from OpenSWATH. I would like to test to see what to fix for better results. 

Thanks,
Eralp
